_note: A device type for Settings › Light setup › Add an appliance: a new device file (config/room/rf/<id>.json) starts as a copy of this, with its own name, subsystem and RM4 Pro. A colour light on an RF remote (room_service/adapters/rf_light.py). Its remote (owner's photo, 28 Oct): one power button, Fade, Jump, Flash, Pulse, R G B W Y P CYAN, + and -. Jump and Pulse aren't used (other buttons do the same). Fade cycles the colours, so it is a colour of its own. Brightness: 'steps' presses of +/- from black to full (owner, 28 Oct: 9 levels, 0-8; it may only dim white). 'repeat': buttons whose Test keeps sending while held, as the remote does. The room keeps its own record and presses buttons in order, gap_s apart; a colour change goes down to black, the colour, then back up. After power at the wall it comes on white at full: Reset (white, down x steps, power off). 'clean': each press is sent as a clean packet (one copy of the learned code, frames times, then gap_ms of silence) rather than the raw ~0.7 s capture, which the far pinspot missed when presses came quickly (28 Oct). 'held': Hold + / Hold − (the remote's + and − held down). A fade is the code sent over and over without a break, as the remote does while held (the light steps ~10 times a second while it keeps coming): one packet of as many copies as the RM4 Pro takes (~0.95 s), at the learned 433.57 MHz (an RM4 Pro recording is 0xb1 0xc0, length, then the frequency in kHz). hold_s 0: that one packet; more: further packets (with ~0.2 s gaps).
description: A colour light on a radio remote: power, seven colours and the colour cycle, brightness from black to full, and flash (strobe). Several on one remote work as one.
